Subject: Next steps after demo — numbers we need

Hi Camila,

Thanks again for the walkthrough yesterday — the demo helped us understand latency and the caching primitives in Redwood. The stakeholders here want two things so we can move procurement forward: a compact economics document that shows (1) a conservative estimate of savings from enabling prefix/KV caching and batching at our likely throughput (approx 1.2M tokens/month), and (2) a recommendation on quantization strategy for our model mix (we're running a custom 13B + some LLM ensemble).

From: Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.com>

Date: Sat, 28 Mar 2026 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Next steps after demo — numbers we need

Sophie — great to hear. I pulled together a concise pack (attached) and sketched three options below; I focused on conservative savings and clear guardrails so procurement can evaluate. Spreadsheet attached: optkit-pricing-breakdown.xlsx; technical appendix: optkit-quantization-recommendations.pdf

High-level (conservative assumptions):
- Pilot (30–60 days): $25k credits, pre-configured prefix caching for chat, 2x burst capacity for onboarding. Estimated savings vs. baseline (no cache, 1:1 token cost): ~18–22% on our conservative run rate.
- Commit band (12 months): Commit $150k -> blended unit discount ~12% + caching-enabled runtime; expected savings 25–32% depending on cache hit rate. Includes priority support and monthly health check.
- Scale/Hybrid (24 months): Commit $350k -> additional quantization enablement (int8 runtime where acceptable) + automated batching optimizations -> up to 38% effective unit cost reduction in mixed workloads.

Quantization notes (short):
- Recommendation: start with mixed FP16 / NVidia TF32 production slices and test int8 on non-critical, high-volume endpoints. Int8 can save ~25–35% on GPU cost per token but requires evaluation on your ensemble for fidelity.
- Hardware guidance: H100 with int8 provides best raw unit spend; A100 + int8 is viable with lower throughput but easier migration.

Operational caveats:
- KV cache hit-rate variability is the primary lever — we used a conservative 42% hit rate in these numbers. If your usage is chat-heavy with many repetitive prompts, expect higher.
- Batching adds latency variance; we suggested routing critical low-latency routes to a lower-batch, higher-cost lane.

Next steps I propose: a 45-minute econ workshop Tues/Wed (we can run the savings simulation live), followed by a formal mutual action plan (MAP) and a DocuSign-friendly term sheet.

I've attached the spreadsheet and the short quant recommendations PDF. Let me know an available slot and I'll loop in Aditya and Markus for pricing governance/discount approvals.

Best,
Camila Reyes
Principal Sales Lead, Redwood Inference

Attachments: optkit-pricing-breakdown.xlsx; optkit-quantization-recommendations.pdf

Hi Sophie / Procurement — looping in pricing. Quick answers inline (and attaching a MAP template for clarity).

- Recurring vs one-time: pilot credits are one-time ($25k) to be consumed within 60 days. Commit bands are recurring pre-pay buckets that draw down monthly. Transactional overages bill at list rate unless the commit is exceeded (we'll apply the blended discount). See spreadsheet tab "cashflow".

- SLA / exceptions: Standard hosted SLA: 99.5% monthly uptime with service credits scaled by effective downtime. Exception clause: quantized int8 runtime is considered an "optimized runtime" — we include it as GA in the commit offer, but our support playbook disclaims fidelity regressions. If a customer requests rollback to FP16 for production incidents, rollback is supported and we will not apply SLA credits for issues caused by model-level fidelity changes. We called that out explicitly on page 2 of the attachment.

- Introductory concession: We can offer a first-year accelerator: additional 8% rebate applied as a one-time credit at 6 months if consumption hits 80% of the committed band. Alternatively, we can convert that concession into an extra $15k in pilot credits (useful for E2E validation).

Operational guardrail we recommend: enable KV prefix caching on conversational flows that meet a 30% repeat-prompt threshold and keep latency-sensitive endpoints on a dedicated low-batch profile. That reduces cost predictably and keeps tail latency SLAs stable.

I've attached the mutual action plan (finlayer-map-mvp.mpp) and flagged the MAP milestones that map to credits and rollout. If the procurement team confirms preference (rebate vs extra pilot credits) we'll wire the terms for DocuSign.

Best,
Aditya Rao
Head of Commercial, Redwood Inference

Attachments: finlayer-map-mvp.mpp
